frontmatter.name: power-automate-execution-layer
frontmatter.description: Cowork/Copilot Studio skill: use Power Automate as a governed execution layer when a locked-down Microsoft agent lacks a direct tool, connector, or permission scope for an admin, business, SaaS, database, HTTP API, on-prem, or cross-system action. First look for an existing helper flow. If none exists and the task is repeatable, admin-scope, or cross-system, build a helper flow, run it, inspect the run, and report the run ID.

frontmatter.name: power-automate-build
frontmatter.description: Build, scaffold, and deploy Power Automate cloud flows using the FlowStudio MCP server. Your agent constructs flow definitions, wires connections, deploys, and tests — all via MCP without opening the portal. Load this skill when asked to: create a flow, build a new flow, deploy a flow definition, scaffold a Power Automate workflow, construct a flow JSON, update an existing flow's actions, patch a flow definition, add actions to a flow, wire up connections, or generate a workflow definition from scratch. Requires the Flow Studio Power Automate connector to be enabled and connected from Cowork Sources & Skills.

frontmatter.name: power-automate-debug
frontmatter.description: Debug failing Power Automate cloud flows using the FlowStudio MCP server. The Graph API only shows top-level status codes. This skill gives your agent action-level inputs and outputs to find the actual root cause. Load this skill when asked to: debug a flow, investigate a failed run, why is this flow failing, inspect action outputs, find the root cause of a flow error, fix a broken Power Automate flow, diagnose a timeout, trace a DynamicOperationRequestFailure, check connector auth errors, read error details from a run, or troubleshoot expression failures. Requires the Flow Studio Power Automate connector to be enabled and connected from Cowork Sources & Skills.

frontmatter.name: power-automate-mcp
frontmatter.description: Foundation skill for Power Automate via FlowStudio MCP — auth setup, the reusable MCP helper (Python + Node.js), tool discovery via `list_skills` / `tool_search`, and oversized-response handling. Load this skill first when connecting an agent to Power Automate. For specialized workflows, load `power-automate-execution-layer`, `power-automate-build`, or `power-automate-debug` — each contains the workflow narrative, this skill provides the plumbing they all rely on. Requires the Flow Studio Power Automate connector to be enabled and connected from Cowork Sources & Skills.

agentConnectors.description: Use Power Automate as Cowork's governed execution layer. Build, run, inspect, and repair helper flows for Microsoft 365 admin tasks, SaaS systems, databases, HTTP APIs, and on-prem systems when direct tools or scopes are missing. Requires Flow Studio MCP setup at mcp.flowstudio.app: claim Starter or a paid plan, then connect Power Automate and Power Apps.

tools.name: tool_search
tools.description: PREFER THIS over guessing tool names when picking from this server. Searches Flow Studio MCP tools by keyword, skill bundle, or explicit selector and returns full JSON schemas for matched tools so they can be called immediately. Call this whenever the user request maps to functionality you are not 100% sure about, OR when you want to load a whole skill bundle (build-flow, debug-flow, discover) at once. Query forms: (1) "skill:<name>" — fetch the full bundle (use list_skills first to see options); (2) "select:name1,name2" — fetch exact tools by name; (3) free-text keywords like "cancel run" or "trigger url" — ranked match against tool name + description. Non-billable.

query.description: Search query. Forms: "select:name1,name2", "skill:<name>", or free-text keywords.

max_results.description: Max tools to return for keyword queries (default 5). Ignored for select: and skill: queries.

tools.name: list_skills
tools.description: List all skill bundles — named groups of tools the agent typically uses together for a single user intent (build-flow, debug-flow, discover). Returns each skill's description and member tool names. Call this first when you are unsure which tools apply to a request; then call tool_search with query: "skill:<name>" to load the full bundle. Non-billable.

tools.name: get_live_flow_trigger_url
tools.description: [DEPRECATED — scheduled for removal] Fetch the live trigger URL and method for an HTTP-triggered flow directly from the Power Automate API. Unlike get_flow_trigger_url this calls the PA listCallbackUrl endpoint so the URL is always current. Returns triggerName, triggerType, triggerKind, triggerMethod (e.g. POST) and triggerUrl. For non-HTTP triggers, triggerMethod and triggerUrl are null.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

tools.name: get_live_flow_runs
tools.description: Fetch live run history for a flow directly from the Power Automate API using impersonation. Returns run name, status, startTime, endTime, trigger name/code, and any top-level error.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

top.description: Max runs to return. Paginates automatically. Default 30.

tools.name: get_live_flow_run_error
tools.description: Fetch error details for a specific flow run from the live Power Automate API. Lists every failed action with its error code and message to help diagnose what went wrong.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

top.description: Max actions to return. Paginates automatically. Omit for all.

tools.name: get_live_flow_run_action_outputs
tools.description: Download inputs and outputs for actions in a flow run via SAS blob links from the live Power Automate API. Without actionName: returns top-level actions (optionally filtered by name). With actionName: calls the PA repetitions endpoint to return every execution of that action across all foreach iterations. Each repetition record includes repetitionIndexes (scope name + itemIndex per nesting level), status, error, and the resolved inputs/outputs blobs. Use iterationIndex to pin to a single iteration (matched against the innermost repetitionIndexes[].itemIndex); omit it to return all repetitions.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

actionName.description: Action name. Without iterationIndex: returns all repetitions of this action across every foreach iteration. With iterationIndex: returns the single repetition matching that iteration. Omit entirely for top-level action list.

iterationIndex.description: Zero-based foreach iteration index. Matched against the innermost repetitionIndexes[].itemIndex in the PA repetition record. Only meaningful when actionName is also set.

top.description: Max actions or repetitions to return. Paginates automatically. Omit for all.

tools.name: trigger_live_flow
tools.description: Trigger an HTTP-triggered Power Automate flow by calling its live callback URL. Fetches the current signed trigger URL via the PA API (listCallbackUrl) then POSTs the provided body to it. If the flow trigger requires Azure Active Directory authentication, the impersonated Bearer token is automatically included — no extra configuration needed. Returns the HTTP status, response body, requiresAadAuth flag, and authType. Only works for flows with a Request (HTTP) trigger type.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

body.description: JSON body to POST to the trigger URL. Omit for flows that expect an empty body.

tools.name: cancel_live_flow_run
tools.description: Cancel a currently running Power Automate flow run via the live PA API. Use after get_live_flow_runs to obtain the run name. Only runs with status "Running" can be cancelled.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

tools.name: resubmit_live_flow_run
tools.description: Resubmit a failed or cancelled Power Automate flow run via the live PA API, re-using the original trigger payload. Discovers the trigger name from the flow definition automatically — no trigger name parameter needed.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

tools.name: set_live_flow_state
tools.description: Start or stop a Power Automate flow via the live Power Automate API using an impersonated service account. Does not require a Power Clarity workspace — works for any flow the impersonated account can access. Reads the current flow state first and only issues the start/stop call if a state change is actually needed. Returns the flow name, environment, requested state, and the actual state reported by the PA API after the operation.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

tools.name: get_live_flow
tools.description: Fetch the full native Power Automate flow JSON from the PA API, including the complete flow definition (triggers, actions, parameters, outputs). Returns the raw properties object exactly as the PA API returns it. Use this to inspect the full definition before calling update_live_flow with a modified definition.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

tools.name: update_live_flow
tools.description: Update or create a Power Automate flow via the live PA API. If flowName is omitted or blank, a new flow is created (PUT with a generated GUID) using an environment admin account — definition and displayName are required in that case. If flowName is provided, the existing flow is PATCHed: displayName and/or definition and/or connectionReferences are updated. Mirrors displayName changes into the Power Clarity cache. To modify a definition: call get_live_flow, mutate properties.definition (including its description), pass it here. The flow description lives at definition.description and is required; we append " #flowstudio-mcp" to it for usage tracking.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

flowName.description: Name (ID) of the flow to update. Omit or leave blank to create a new flow.

displayName.description: Display name for the flow. Required when creating.

definition.description: Full flow definition as a JSON object (triggers + actions + parameters + outputs + description). MUST be a JSON object — strings are rejected. Do not JSON.stringify the definition; pass the parsed object directly. Required when creating. For updates, obtain from get_live_flow (properties.definition), modify it, then pass the modified object here. definition.description is required (a short note about what changed); when updating, if you omit it we reuse the flow's existing description.

connectionReferences.description: Connection references map — keyed by logical name (e.g. shared_sharepointonline), each value is { connectionName, id }. Goes into properties.connectionReferences on the PA API call.

tools.name: get_live_flow_http_schema
tools.description: [DEPRECATED — scheduled for removal] Inspect the HTTP interface of a Power Automate Request-triggered flow: returns the JSON schema the trigger URL expects as the POST body, any required headers, the HTTP method, and the JSON schema(s) defined on any Response action(s) in the flow. All information is read from the live flow definition via the PA API — no test call is made to the trigger URL. Use this before calling trigger_live_flow to understand what body to send.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

tools.name: list_live_environments
tools.description: List all Power Platform environments directly from the Power Automate API. Returns id, displayName, sku, location, and state for each environment visible to the impersonated service account.

top.description: Max environments to return. Paginates automatically. Omit for all.

tools.name: list_live_flows
tools.description: List Power Automate flows in an environment. Returns id, displayName, state, triggerType, and lastModifiedTime for each flow. mode=owner (default): flows owned by the impersonated account, with full definition. mode=admin: all flows in the environment (requires an admin account). If search is provided, results are filtered to flows whose displayName contains the search text. For large environments pagination is time-bounded — if nextLink is returned, pass it as continuationUrl to retrieve the next batch.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

mode.description: owner (default): user-scoped endpoint, owned flows only with full definitions. admin: admin-scoped endpoint, all flows.

top.description: Max flows to return. Paginates automatically. Omit for all.

search.description: Optional case-insensitive filter applied to flow displayName.

continuationUrl.description: nextLink value returned by a previous call. Pass to resume pagination from where the last call stopped. Must match the same mode as the original call.

timeoutSeconds.description: Stop collecting pages after this many seconds and return a nextLink for the next batch. Default 25. Max 55.

tools.name: list_live_connections
tools.description: List Power Platform connections in an environment directly from the Power Automate API. Returns id, displayName, connectorName, environment, createdBy (full object), authenticatedUser, statuses, overallStatus, createdTime, expirationTime, and connectionParameters for each connection. Pass search=<term> to narrow the list and receive a paste-ready connectionReferenceTemplate plus action-side hostTemplate per connection — drop these into update_live_flow's connectionReferences and inputs.host without further edits.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment. Omit to list connections across all environments.

top.description: Max connections to return. Paginates automatically. Omit for all.

search.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter applied to id, displayName, connectorName, and accountName. Adds connectionReferenceTemplate + hostTemplate to each returned connection.

tools.name: describe_live_connector
tools.description: Describe a live Power Platform connector/API and its operations. Aligned with Canvas MCP describe_api. Use mode=summary (default) to get a compact operation catalog. Use operationId to describe one operation, including inputs, outputs, dynamic parameter metadata, nextTool hints to call get_live_dynamic_options, and an authored hint + canonical example shape (when one exists) to copy into update_live_flow. Use search without connectorName/apiName to search operations across connectors and get connection-aware suggestions. Use mode=full only when raw OpenAPI connector metadata is required.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

connectorName.description: Connector logical name, for example shared_teams. Either connectorName/apiName is required, unless search is provided for cross-connector operation search.

apiName.description: Alias for connectorName, matching Canvas MCP describe_api naming.

mode.description: summary (default): compact operation catalog. full: raw OpenAPI metadata.

operationId.description: Optional operation ID to describe with expanded inputs and outputs.

type.description: Operation usage to include in summary mode. Default Action.

search.description: Optional operation search text. With connectorName, filters that connector summary. Without connectorName, searches operations across connectors.

top.description: Max operations to return in connector summary mode, or max top search results to show in cross-connector search. Default 250 for summary, 10 for search display.

variant.description: When an operation has multiple authored variants (e.g. shared_teams/PostMessageToConversation has channel/groupchat/flowbot_chat), pass a specific variantKey to get that variant's hint and exampleDefinition. Omit to receive a hint listing the available variants.

tools.name: get_live_dynamic_options
tools.description: Resolve live dynamic dropdown/list options for a connector operation parameter. Use this when describe_live_connector returns a dynamic parameter with nextTool=get_live_dynamic_options. Works with x-ms-dynamic-list and x-ms-dynamic-values metadata, for example Teams team/channel IDs, SharePoint site/list IDs, or other connector-specific selectable values.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

connectorName.description: Connector logical name, for example shared_teams.

operationId.description: Operation ID that owns the dynamic parameter.

parameterName.description: Dynamic parameter name, for example groupId or channelId.

connectionName.description: Required connector connection name/id, for example shared-teams-{guid}. Choose the connection that the flow action should run as. Use list_live_connections to find candidates.

parameters.description: Resolved dependent parameter values, for example { "groupId": "<team id>" }.

dynamicMetadata.description: x-ms-dynamic-list or x-ms-dynamic-values metadata from describe_live_connector.

search.description: Optional displayName or value search. Returns bestMatch when found.

tools.name: get_live_dynamic_properties
tools.description: Resolve live dynamic schema/properties for a connector operation parameter. Use this when describe_live_connector returns a dynamicProperties entry with nextTool=get_live_dynamic_properties. Works with x-ms-dynamic-properties and x-ms-dynamic-schema metadata, for example SharePoint item fields after resolving site/list/view parameters.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

connectorName.description: Connector logical name, for example shared_sharepointonline.

operationId.description: Operation ID that owns the dynamic parameter.

parameterName.description: Dynamic properties parameter name, for example item or body.

connectionName.description: Required connector connection name/id. Use list_live_connections to find candidates.

parameters.description: Resolved dependent parameter values, for example { "dataset": "<site url>", "table": "<list id>" }.

dynamicMetadata.description: x-ms-dynamic-properties or x-ms-dynamic-schema metadata from describe_live_connector.

contextParameterAlias.description: Alias for returned property paths. Defaults to the parameter alias from metadata, or parameterName.

location.description: Whether to resolve input or output dynamic properties. Default input.

propertyName.description: Optional property name/title/alias to return just one property. Useful for a progressive follow-up with includeRaw=true after inspecting the compact schema.

includeRaw.description: Include raw schema/property definitions. With propertyName, includes raw only for the matched property. Without propertyName, includes the full raw schema. Default false.

tools.name: add_live_flow_to_solution
tools.description: Migrate a non-solution Power Automate flow into a solution via the admin migrateFlows API. If the flow is already part of a solution, returns an error message without attempting migration. solutionId is optional — omit to migrate into the default solution.

environmentName.description: Name of the Power Platform environment.

flowName.description: Name (ID) of the flow to migrate into the solution.

solutionId.description: Target solution ID. Omit to migrate into the default solution.

titles.longDescription:
Flow Studio MCP Copilot Cowork connects Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork to the Flow Studio MCP server, giving authorized users a governed way to work with Power Automate cloud flows from natural language.

You can discover flows, inspect definitions, review run history, diagnose failed runs with action-level details, and build or update flows using your configured Flow Studio and Microsoft Power Platform connections.

Getting started

  1. Sign up at mcp.flowstudio.app — claim a free Starter plan or a paid plan
  2. Install this plugin in Cowork and sign in with your Microsoft 365 account

Resources

  • Flow Studio MCP Copilot Cowork plugin setup guide
  • When to use which agent
  • MCP tools reference
  • FAQ
  • Contact support

Requirements: A Flow Studio MCP plan (Starter is free). Multi-tenant - works in any Microsoft 365 organization.

Flow Studio MCP also works with Copilot Studio agents, Claude, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and other MCP-compatible clients via direct configuration. This plugin specifically enables the Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork integration.

tools.name: renameFileOrFolderInMyOnedrive
tools.description: Use this tool for the user's personal OneDrive only.Rename a file or a folder in the user's OneDrive.

etag.description:
ETag value for concurrency control via the HTTP 'If-Match' header.
Before calling this tool, first call getFileOrFolderMetadataInMyOnedrive to fetch the latest ETag for this driveItem, and do not reuse an older ETag from an earlier step.
Rename succeeds only if the driveItem's current ETag matches.
If the ETag is stale or does not match, the operation returns 412 Precondition Failed.

tools.name: getFolderChildrenInMyOnedrive
tools.description: Enumerates Top 20 files and folders (DriveItems) contained within a specified parent folder in the user's personal OneDrive.

parentFolderId.description: ID of the parent folder (DriveItem) whose files and folders will be listed.Defaults to the root folder of the user's OneDrive if not specified.

tools.name: shareFileOrFolderInMyOnedrive
tools.description: Send a sharing invitation for a file or folder in the user's personal OneDrive. Supports assigning roles (read/write) and notifying recipients.

fileOrFolderId.description: ID of the file or folder (DriveItem) to share.

recipientEmails.description: Email addresses of recipients to invite.At least one recipient email is required.

roles.description: Roles to assign to recipients.Accepted values: read, write (write grants both read and write access).Defaults to read role if not specified.

sendInvitation.description: Indicates whether to send a sharing invitation.Defaults to true if not specified.

message.description: Custom message to include in the invitation email.Defaults to a standard message if not specified.
message.default: Here's the file we're collaborating on.

tools.name: setSensitivityLabelOnFileInMyOnedrive
tools.description: Set the sensitivity label of a file in the user's personal OneDrive.

fileId.description: The file id (also known as driveItemId) of the file in the user's OneDrive

sensitivityLabelId.description: Required.ID of the sensitivity label to be assigned, or empty string to remove the sensitivity label.

assignmentMethod.description: Optional.The assignment method of the label on the document.Indicates whether the assignment of the label was done automatically, standard,or as a privileged operation (the equivalent of an administrator operation).Possible values are standard, privileged, auto and unknownFutureValue.

justificationText.description: Optional.Justification text for audit purposes, and is required when downgrading/removing a label.

tools.name: createSmallTextFileInMyOnedrive
tools.description: Create or upload a text file under 5MB to the user's personal OneDrive.

tools.name: findFileOrFolderInMyDrive
tools.description: Find a file or folder in the user's OneDrive by search query.

searchQuery.description: Search query could be the entire or partial file name.

tools.name: getFileOrFolderMetadataInMyOnedrive
tools.description: Get metadata of a file or a folder (also referred to as DriveItems) from the user's personal OneDrive.

titles.longDescription:
enosix arnold™ for Copilot Cowork brings SAP ERP data directly into Microsoft 365 Copilot. Sales teams, customer service representatives, and operations staff can query live SAP data, track orders and deliveries, and initiate document workflows — all without leaving Copilot Chat.

What this app does

  • Order Search — Find open or historical sales orders by customer name, material, or date range.
  • Order Status & Availability — Check delivery status for an order and confirm material stock levels in real time.
  • Billing & Invoice Lookup — Retrieve SAP billing documents and invoice totals for a customer over a date range.
  • Delivery Document Lookup — View outbound delivery documents, shipping status, and delivery dates.
  • PDF Document Download — Generate and download SAP sales order, delivery, invoice, and quote PDFs.
  • Order Cancellation Check — Determine whether a sales order is still eligible for cancellation based on its fulfillment status.
  • Order Update Feasibility — Verify whether a sales order can be modified before requesting a change.
  • Order Quantity Update — Change or cancel a sales order line item quantity directly from Copilot Chat.
  • Quote Creation via Cloud UI — Initiate a new SAP quote for a customer through the enosix Arnold Cloud UI application.

How it works

The app connects to an enosix Arnold MCP server using OAuth 2.0 authentication. Copilot Cowork authenticates once using your Microsoft 365 identity; subsequent sessions refresh automatically. Your SAP data is never replicated — it stays in place in your SAP system and is accessed in real time through the arnold™ platform, with no data replication.

All results are returned directly in Copilot Chat. For richer workflows, arnold™ also supports real-time document reprinting — generating live PDFs of sales orders, invoices, deliveries, and quotes on demand — and integrated Cloud UI components that launch in-context for transactional work like quote and order creation.

Built for enterprise security

enosix Arnold is hosted on Microsoft Azure using managed services and secured through Microsoft Entra ID. Single Sign-On (SSO) and SAP Principal Propagation ensure that every transaction carries the user's SAP identity — preserving document audit trails and enforcing SAP role-based access controls exactly as configured.

Who it's for

Designed for enterprise sales, customer service, and operations teams at organizations running SAP ECC or SAP S/4HANA. Industries that benefit include manufacturing, distribution, life sciences, energy, and any SAP-driven enterprise looking to surface ERP data where work happens. This app is intended for use by employees with an active Microsoft 365 Copilot seat and access to a connected enosix Arnold subscription.

Requirements and account setup

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot license
  • enosix Arnold subscription with a connected SAP ECC or SAP S/4HANA system

Get started

  • Sign up / Request a demo: https://go.enosix.com/arnold-signup
  • Documentation & Get Started guide: https://go.enosix.com/docs
  • Contact support: https://go.enosix.com/support
  • Privacy policy: https://go.enosix.com/app-privacy-policy

External workflows

Most functionality is delivered directly in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Two workflows involve content outside of Chat:

  • PDF document download — When a PDF is generated for a sales order, invoice, delivery, or quote, Copilot returns a download link. Clicking the link opens the PDF in your web browser, outside of Teams.
  • Quote creation via Cloud UI — Advanced quote configuration (adding line items, entering PO references) is completed in the enosix Arnold Cloud UI, which opens in a separate browser tab outside of Teams.

crossCurrency.description: A comma-separated string of cross currency pairs, each expressed in ISO 4217 alphabetical format (e.g., 'EURCHF,USDJPY'). Each pair must be 6 uppercase letters.

dealAmount.description: Amount of the deal (base) currency bought or sold

referenceCurrency.description: Reference currency for cross-currency calculations (ISO 4217 format, e.g., 'USD', 'EUR'). Use this when pricing non-major currency pairs 'via' a major currency (e.g., NOK/SEK via EUR).

startDate.description: The start date of the instrument. Possible values are: AdjustableDate object - requires a date expressed in ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., "2021-01-01"). Or a RelativeAdjustableDate - requires a tenor expressed as a code indicating the period between referenceDate(default=startDate) to endDate of the instrument (e.g., "ON" for overnight, "TN" for tomorrow-next, "1W", "30D", "6M", "1Y"). Default is a spot date.

endDate.description: The maturity date of the instrument. Possible values are:AdjustableDate object - requires a date expressed in ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., "2021-01-01"). Or a RelativeAdjustableDate - requires a tenor expressed as a code indicating the period between referenceDate(default=startDate) to endDate of the instrument (e.g., "ON" for overnight, "TN" for tomorrow-next, "1W", "30D", "6M", "1Y").

code.description: A comma-separated string of bond future identifiers (RIC or other instrument code). Examples: 'YTTc1' for single bond future or 'YTTc1,YTTc2' for multiple bond futures

marketDataDate.description: Market data date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD) for pricing (defaults to today if not specified). It is usually defined if the pricing must be done in the past.

tools.name: option_value
tools.title: Pricer: Option
tools.description: Calculate option valuation and analytics using LSEG Option API v1. Provides detailed risk metrics including Delta (price sensitivity), Gamma (delta sensitivity), Theta (time decay), Vega (volatility sensitivity), and Rho (interest rate sensitivity). Supports vanilla options (European, American, Bermudan), exotic barrier options (knock-in/knock-out with rebates), binary options for FX (OneTouch, NoTouch, Digital with fixed payouts), and Asian options (price/strike averaging with arithmetic/geometric calculation). Calculates market values, intrinsic values, time premiums, implied volatility, hedge ratios, leverage, moneyness ratios, premium over cash, and annualized yields.

code.description: Existing option identifier (ISIN, RIC). If provided, this takes precedence over definition-based inputs.

definition.description: The full definition of the option

underlyingCode.description: The code used to define the underlying asset (e.g., 'AAPL.O' for Apple equity, 'VOD.L' for Vodafone equity, 'EURUSD' for EUR/USD FX, 'GBPCAD' for GBP/CAD FX)

optionType.description: Whether the option is a call or put

strike.description: The strike price at which the option holder can buy or sell the underlying asset. Note: This field should NOT be provided for Asian options with asianType='Strike' as the strike will be determined by the average price. It should also not be set for Fx binary options.

exerciseStyle.description: Exercise timing rules determining when option can be exercised and affecting pricing complexity. Note: This field should NOT be provided for Asian options as they use automatic exercise style determination.

notionalAmount.description: The notional amount of the option. This is field is used only for FX options to define the contract size, and is not supported for Equity options. It should also not be set for Fx binary options.

notionalCurrency.description: The currency of the notional amount (ISO 4217 format). This field is used only for FX options, and is not applicable for Equity options. It should also not be set for Fx binary options.

endDate.description: The maturity/expiry date of the option (ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD)

currency.description: The currency in which the amount is expressed (ISO 4217 format)

barrierDown.description: An object that defines a down barrier option

inOrOut.description: The type of a barrier option based on whether it is activated or deactivated when the price of the underlying asset reaches a certain barrier

level.description: The price used as a barrier level

binaryType.description: The type of a binary option based on the trigger that activates it

level.description: The price used as a binary option level

payoutAmount.description: An object that specifies the amount and the currency in which it is expressed

currency.description: The currency in which the amount is expressed (ISO 4217 format)

paymentType.description: The type of a binary option based on when it is paid out

asian.description: Asian option specification with path-dependent payoffs based on price averaging over observation period. Strike field rules: Asian Price options REQUIRE strike field (average price determines payoff), Asian Strike options PROHIBIT strike field (average price becomes strike). Supports both FX and Equity underlyings with flexible averaging methods (arithmetic/geometric) and optional custom fixing schedules.

asianType.description: The type of an Asian option based on whether the strike is fixed or not

averageType.description: The mathematical type used to calculate the average price of the underlying asset

fixingSchedule.description: Optional schedule specification for Asian option price observation dates that defines when underlying asset prices are sampled for averaging calculations. If not provided, uses default market conventions based on option tenor and underlying type. Custom schedules enable precise control over observation frequency, start/end dates, and sampling patterns. Critical for accurate Asian option valuation as observation methodology significantly impacts final payoff calculations and option pricing.

startDate.description: Optional start date of the observation schedule in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). If not defined, the schedule is spot-starting and default start date is determined based on market conventions for the underlying asset type. Early start dates increase sampling frequency and reduce averaging volatility.

endDate.description: End date of the observation schedule in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD) defining the final fixing date for price averaging. Typically aligns with or precedes the option expiration date. Longer observation periods generally reduce option volatility and premium.

frequency.description: Frequency of price observations during the regular observation period affecting sampling density and averaging accuracy. Common frequencies include Daily (Everyday, EveryWorkingDay), Weekly (Every7Days), Monthly, Quarterly, and specialized frequencies for different market conventions. Higher frequency reduces manipulation risk but may increase transaction costs.

tools.title: Pricer: Swap
tools.description:
**THIS IS A QPS TOOL — NOT YIELDBOOK. If the user mentions "yieldbook" anywhere in their request, you MUST NOT use this tool. Use fixed_income_risk_analytics instead.**
        Two-phase IR Swap tool: (1) Call with currency (+ optional swapType/indexName) to list available swap templates, (2) Call with swaps array to price swaps using templates. Returns template info or pricing results with risk metrics.

currency.description: Currency code to filter templates (e.g., EUR, USD, GBP, CHF). Required for listing templates.

swapType.description: Filter by swap type (for listing) or specify swap type (for pricing)

indexName.description: Filter by floating rate index name (e.g., ESTR, SOFR, EURIBOR, SONIA). Used for listing only.

swaps.description: Array of swap pricing requests. Provide this to price swaps instead of listing templates.

reference.description: Template reference from template list (e.g., 'LSEG/EUR_AB3E' or UUID)

swapType.description: Type of swap (must match template type). Use VanillaSwap for standard fixed-float, TenorBasisSwap for tenor basis, CurrencyBasisSwap for currency basis, CrossCurrencySwap for cross-currency.

startDate.description: Start date in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD) or tenor (e.g., '1M', '2Y'). If omitted, uses template default.

endDate.description: End date in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD) or tenor (e.g., '5Y', '10Y'). If omitted, uses template default.

spread.description: Spread in basis points (only for vanilla/cross-currency swaps). If omitted, uses template default (typically 0).

amount.description: Notional amount in base currency. If omitted, uses template default (typically 1,000,000).

valuationDate.description: Valuation date in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD). Used for pricing only. Defaults to today if omitted.

tools.name: interest_rate_curve
tools.title: MktData: Interest Rate Curve
tools.description: Two-phase Interest Rate Curve tool: (1) Call with listOnly=true to see available curves, (2) Call with reference to calculate curve points. Can also call directly with reference if already known.

listOnly.description: Set to true to list available interest rate curves. If false or omitted, will calculate curve points using reference parameter.

reference.description: The identifier of a resource (instrument definition, curve definition) that is already in the platform. Required when listOnly is false or omitted.

tools.name: credit_curve
tools.title: MktData: Credit Curve
tools.description: Two-phase Credit Curve tool: (1) Call with country + issuerType to list curves. For Corporate, also provide at least one filter: name, sector, rating, or currency. Returns columnar {columns, rows}. (2) Call with id + name to calculate curve points.

country.description: Country code of the issuer defined with Alpha-2 Code ISO 3166 country code convention.

issuerType.description: Type of the issuer. Available values are: Agency, Corporate, Munis, NonFinancials, Sovereign, Supranational.

id.description: The ID (GUID) of an existing credit curve definition.

name.description: In list mode: case-insensitive substring filter on curve name (e.g. 'Goldman Sachs'). In calculate mode: the exact name of the curve definition (required with id).

sector.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on economic sector (e.g. 'Healthcare', 'Technology'). Only valid in list mode.

rating.description: Exact credit rating filter, case-insensitive (e.g. 'BBB', 'AA'). Only valid in list mode.

currency.description: Exact currency code filter, case-insensitive (e.g. 'USD', 'EUR'). Only valid in list mode.

tools.name: inflation_curve
tools.title: MktData: Inflation Curve
tools.description: Two-phase Inflation Curve tool: (1) Call without id/name to list/search available curves (optionally filter by country/currency), (2) Call with id and/or name to calculate curve points.

country.description: The country code of the curve origin. The value is defined with Alpha-2 Code ISO 3166 country code convention (e.g., 'US'). Used for listing/searching only.

currency.description: The currency code of the curve. The value is expressed in ISO 4217 alphabetical format (e.g., 'USD'). Used for listing/searching only.

id.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of an existing inflation curve definition. Used for calculation. Provide id and/or name to calculate.

name.description: The name of an existing inflation curve definition. Used for calculation. Provide id and/or name to calculate.

tools.name: fx_forward_curve

tools.description: Two-phase FX Forward Curve tool: (1) Call with listOnly=true to see available curves, (2) Call with reference to calculate curve points. Can also call directly with reference if already known.

listOnly.description: Set to true to list available FX forward curves. If false or omitted, will calculate curve points using reference parameter.

reference.description: The identifier of a resource (instrument definition, curve definition) that is already in the platform. Required when listOnly is false or omitted.

tools.name: qa_ibes_consensus
tools.title: QA: Equity Consensus
tools.description: Primary source for forward-looking QA IBES analyst data. Use qa_ibes_consensus for future fiscal guidance (e.g., Rev FY25-27), qa_ibes_actuals for reported historical results, and qa_ibes_measures for metadata. Always submit a requests array with entries specifying dataType (qa_ibes_consensus | qa_ibes_actuals | qa_ibes_measures) and matching options.

requests.description: One or more QA IBES operations. Each entry selects a subtool via dataType.

options.title: QA IBES Consensus Options
options.description:
Retrieves IBES (Institutional Brokers' Estimate System) analyst consensus estimates for requested fiscal periods, past or future.
Returns consensus metrics including the normalized mean estimate for each requested measure (sales/revenue, earnings, cash flow, dividends, etc.).
This is the correct tool when a user asks for forward-looking guidance ("FY25-27 revenue outlook", "next quarter EPS") because it provides projected consensus, not reported statements.
For each fiscal period, the endpoint returns the latest published consensus values.
Note: historical requests (negative periodIndex) still return consensus snapshots—use the dedicated actual endpoint to retrieve reported IBES actuals.
Supply a ticker, one or more measures (such as Cfps, Dps, Epsebg, Eps, Ffops, Pprofit, Rev but not limited to those),
and optionally periodIndexStart / periodIndexEnd (integers where 0 = latest reported period, 1 = next forward period, negatives = history)
plus periodType (Quarter | Year | HalfYear, default Year). When the user provides a ticker identifier, always try to determine and explicitly pass 
the tickerType parameter. Set tickerType: 'SEDOL' only if the user explicitly mentions 'SEDOL'.
The 'Date' field in the response represents the fiscal period end date, not when the estimate was published.
Fiscal period end dates in the response reflect the issuer's fiscal calendar, so note companies with non-December year-ends when answering "which quarter" questions.
If the user needs reported GAAP/IFRS financials rather than estimates, call qa_company_fundamentals instead.

ticker.description: Security ticker symbol. Example: 'AAPL' for Apple Inc., 'IBM' for International Business Machines, 'MSFT' for Microsoft.

tickerType.description: Optional ticker type hint. Values: Ticker, SEDOL, RIC, CUSIP, ComName, IBESTicker. If ticker type is not specified it looks up for Ticker, RIC, CUSIP, ComName, IBESTicker; and it includes SEDOL along other types only if SEDOL tickerType is requested.

periodIndexStart.description: Optional minimum fiscal period index. Use 0 for the latest reported period, 1 for the next period, negatives for history.

periodIndexEnd.description: Optional maximum fiscal period index. Leave blank to include all periods after periodIndexStart.

measures.description: Measure types to retrieve (required). Provide at least one measure as a comma-separated list, such as, but not limited to, Cfps, Dps, Epsebg, Eps, Ffops, Pprofit, Rev.

periodType.description: Fiscal period type for the estimates (Quarter, Year, or HalfYear).

options.title: QA IBES Actuals Options
options.description:
Returns historical IBES reported results via the /ibes-actual endpoint.
Provide a ticker, one or more measures examples are Cfps, Dps, Epsebg, Eps, Ffops, Pprofit, Rev but not limited to those,
and a non-positive pIndex (0 = most recent period, -1 = prior period, etc.).
When the user provides a ticker identifier, always try to determine and explicitly pass 
the tickerType parameter. Set tickerType: 'SEDOL' only if the user explicitly mentions 'SEDOL'.
Optionally set periodType (Quarter | Year | HalfYear, default Year). The response contains a single
fiscal period with the actual values and announcement metadata, making it useful for
summarizing what the company reported and comparing results against prior expectations.

tickerType.description: Optional ticker type hint. Values: Ticker, SEDOL, RIC, CUSIP, ComName, IBESTicker. If ticker type is not specified it looks up for Ticker, RIC, CUSIP, ComName, IBESTicker; and it includes SEDOL along other types only if SEDOL tickerType is requested.

measures.description: Array of measure codes. Common examples: Cfps, Dps, Epsebg, Eps, Ffops, Pprofit, Rev. Accepts any valid IBES measure code.

pIndex.description: Relative period index (0 = most recent reported period, negative numbers go further back).

options.title: IBES Measures
options.description:
Searches IBES measure metadata (code, description, scale) to help map measure names
before calling the other subtools. Provide an optional case-insensitive search term
(supports * wildcards), limit between 1 and 500 (default 100), and a cursor for
pagination. Use this to discover valid measure codes or refine UI pickers.

search.description: Optional case-insensitive search term. Supports * wildcards.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return (default 100, max 500).

cursor.description: Opaque cursor token from a previous response.

tools.name: qa_macroeconomic
tools.title: QA: Macroeconomic
tools.description:
Access LSEG QA macroeconomic database for historical economic indicators worldwide. Provides time series data, metadata search, and latest observations. HISTORICAL DATA ONLY - No forecasts available.
THREE-PHASE WORKFLOW:
1. DISCOVERY (list) → Search for indicators
2. VERIFICATION → Check units, frequency, date range  
3. RETRIEVAL (latest/series) → Get the data

REQUEST STRUCTURE:
Submit array of requests with dataType and options:
{
  "requests": [
    {"dataType": "list|latest|series", "options": {...}}
  ]
}

DATATYPE: "list" (Search Indicators)
Find indicators by description and/or country.

Parameters:
- mnemonic: Search code with wildcards (e.g., "US*CPI*")
- description: Search description (e.g., "*GDP*", "*unemployment*")
- marketDescription: Search country (e.g., "*united states*", "*china*")
- frequency: Filter by "ANNL", "MONT", "QUAR", "WTH", "WMO", "WWE", "WFR", "WTU", "DWY"
- limit: Max results (default 25, max 200)
- offset: Skip records for pagination

Returns: mnemonic, description, market, frequency, unit, source, startDate
Present as: Markdown table with columns: Mnemonic | Description | Frequency | Unit | Start Date

Example: {"dataType": "list", "options": {"description": "*GDP*", "marketDescription": "*united states*"}}

DATATYPE: "latest" (Current Value)
Get most recent observation for an indicator.

Parameters:
- mnemonic: Exact code from list search (required)

Returns: period, value, unit, frequency, asOf date, revised status

Example: {"dataType": "latest", "options": {"mnemonic": "USI64..XF"}}

DATATYPE: "series" (Time Series)
Retrieve historical data for an indicator.

Parameters:
- mnemonic: Exact code (required)
- from: Start date YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive, optional)
- to: End date YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive, optional)
- limit: Max observations (use 200 for 10+ years)
- order: "asc" (oldest first) or "desc" (newest first, default)
- frequency: Override default - "M", "Q", "A", "W", "D"
- includeRevisions: Include all revisions (default false)

Returns: Array of {period, value, unit, revised, asOf}
Present as: Markdown table with columns: Year/Period | Value (with unit in header)
- Format numbers with thousand separators
- Include currency/percentage in header or values
- Sort chronologically

Tips:
- Use limit: 200 for long series (10+ years)
- Default may return only recent data without date filters
- Check resultCount for total observations

Example: {"dataType": "series", "options": {"mnemonic": "USI64..XF", "from": "2014-11-01", "limit": 200}}

COMMON INDICATORS:

United States:
- GDP (quarterly, billions): USGDP...B
- CPI %YOY (monthly): USI64..XF
- Unemployment % (monthly): USUN%TOTQ
- Fed Funds % (monthly): USI60...
- Non-Farm Payrolls (monthly, thousands): USEMPALLO
- 10Y Treasury % (daily): FRTCM10

Country Codes: US=USA, CN=Canada, UK=UK, BD=Germany, FR=France, CH=China, JP=Japan, BR=Brazil, ES=Spain

Frequency Codes:
- ANNL/A: Annual
- QUAR/Q: Quarterly  
- MONT/M: Monthly
- WFR/W: Weekly
- DWY: Daily

GDP %YOY Patterns:
- China: CHGDP..*C
- Euro Area: EKESNGD&Q
- Germany: BDGDPDEY*
- France: FRGDP..*D
- Spain: ESGDP..*B

GDP PER CAPITA CALCULATION:
NOT directly available - must calculate manually.

Critical Steps:
1. Find both GDP and population indicators via list search
2. VERIFY UNITS before calculating (critical!)
3. Calculate with correct unit conversion

Common Patterns:

US (IMF):
- GDP: USY99B.CB = millions USD (annual)
- Population: USI99Z..O = thousands (annual)
- Formula: (GDP_millions / Pop_thousands) × 1,000
- ⚠️ USI99Z..O has corrupt data 1948-1949 - use 1950+

US (BEA):
- GDP: USGDP...B = billions USD (quarterly, annualized)
- Population: USPOPTOTP = thousands (monthly)
- Formula: (GDP_billions × 1,000) / Pop_thousands

Other Countries:
- IMF pattern: [CC]Y99B.CB (GDP), [CC]I99Z..O (Pop)
- Units vary - always verify actual values
- Cross-reference World Bank/IMF published figures

Always validate result against published sources!

DATE FORMATS IN RESULTS:
- Monthly: "YYYY-MM" (e.g., "2024-01")
- Quarterly: "YYYY-QN" (e.g., "2024-Q3")
- Annual: "YYYY"
- Daily: "YYYY-MM-DD"

MULTIPLE REQUESTS:
Combine requests in one call:
{
  "requests": [
    {"dataType": "list", "options": {"description": "*inflation*", "marketDescription": "*spain*"}},
    {"dataType": "series", "options": {"mnemonic": "USI64..XF", "from": "2024-01-01"}},
    {"dataType": "latest", "options": {"mnemonic": "USUN%TOTQ"}}
  ]
}

LIMITATIONS:
❌ No forecasts or consensus estimates
❌ No real-time data (indicator lag varies)
❌ No market prices (stocks, commodities)
❌ Coverage varies by country/indicator

TROUBLESHOOTING:

"No data available":
- Check startDate - data may not exist for period
- Recent data may not be published yet
- Try broader date range

Unexpected values:
- Verify units (millions vs billions vs thousands)
- Check if values are rates, indices, or absolute numbers
- Validate against known published figures

Limited results:
- Use limit parameter for long series
- May need pagination for very long histories

DATA SOURCES:
National agencies (BLS, BEA, Eurostat), central banks (Fed, ECB), international orgs (IMF, OECD, World Bank), and private providers.

tools.name: qa_company_fundamentals
tools.title: QA: Company Fundamentals
tools.description: Retrieve reported QA company fundamentals (historical financial statements) and measure metadata via dedicated subtools. Do NOT use for forecast questions—forward-looking estimates belong to qa_ibes_consensus.

requests.description: One or more QA company fundamentals operations. Each entry selects a subtool via dataType.

options.title: QA Company Fundamentals Options
options.description:
Retrieve QA Company Fundamentals data by QA Code/identifier for fiscal year(s), measures, and frequency.
Returns reported fiscal period info, financial metrics, and currency details so you can cite historical GAAP/IFRS results.
Supports Net Sales/Revenues, Gross Income, COGS, EPS, DPS, P/E Ratio and Annual/Quarterly/Quarterly Cumulative frequencies.
Use this only for published company filings; if the question asks for forward-looking outlook or analyst expectations, call qa_ibes_consensus instead.

qaCode.description: QA Company Code identifier. Example: 29833 for Apple Inc. Provide either qaCode OR identifier. If both are provided, qaCode takes priority.

identifier.description: Security identifier or company name - Ticker (e.g., 'AAPL'), CUSIP (e.g., '037833100'), SEDOL (e.g., '2046251'), RIC (e.g., 'AAPL.O'), or Company Name (e.g., 'Apple Inc'). If multiple matches are found, an error will provide QA Codes for disambiguation. Mutually exclusive with qaCode.

measures.description: Comma-separated measure IDs to retrieve. Available measures: 1001 (Net Sales/Revenues), 1100 (Gross Income), 1051 (COGS), 5201 (EPS), 5202 (EPS-FPE), 5145 (DPS-L12M), 5101 (DPS), 9102 (P/E Ratio). Default: '1001,1100,5201,5202,5145,5101,9102'.

year.description: Fiscal year(s) to retrieve fundamentals for. Can be a single year (e.g., 2019 or '2019') or multiple years separated by commas (e.g., 2019, 2020 or '2019,2020'). Accepts both number and string formats. This is a mandatory field.

oneOf.description: Single fiscal year as a number. Example: 2019
Single year or comma-separated years as a string. Examples: '2019' or '2019,2020,2021'

freq.description: Frequency code: 'A' for Annual (default), 'Q' for Quarterly, 'R' for Quarterly - Cumulative. Default: 'A'

options.title: Company Fundamentals Measures
options.description: Search Worldscope measure metadata (number, name, units, industry) with optional search term, limit, and cursor for pagination.

search.description: Optional case-insensitive search term. Supports * wildcards.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return (default 100, max 500).

cursor.description: Opaque cursor token from a previous response.

tools.name: important_company_news
tools.title: News: Important Company News
tools.description: USE WHEN: broad newest-first public and private company news retrieval. RETURNS: News stories descending date order. PARAMETERS RULES: * Query rules: NO natural language or keyword queries search. * Must modify parameters between calls to get different results. * Vary `end_dt` to narrow time window or get duplicate results.* Requires one or more company RIC codes (company_rics) or PermIDs (company_perm_ids). * Private companies: PermIDs only; public: RICs or PermIDs.

companyRics.description: list[string], required, public company RIC/edcoid codes

companyPermIds.description: list[string], accepted, public or private company PermIDs

start.description: string, accepted, start date (ISO 8601 format, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ | YYYY-MM-DD)

end.description: string, accepted, end date (ISO 8601 format, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ | YYYY-MM-DD)

headlineOnly.description: Optional: Set to true to return only headlines without full story text. Default is false (returns full story text).

tools.name: news_nl_search
tools.title: News: Natural Language Search
tools.description: USE WHEN: Lexical search for exact or near-exact words expected to appear in story text, such as names, tickers, products, drugs, acronyms, legal terms, or quoted phrases. Best when known wording matters. RETURNS: Matching news stories in descending date order. PARAMETERS RULES: * `nlQuery` should contain literal words or phrases to find in the text. * Do not use abstract themes, long natural-language questions, boolean operators, search syntax, or dates in `nlQuery`. * Use filters for specific companies and dates when available. * Modify `nlQuery` to search different text; modify filters/date range to change scope.

nlQuery.description: string, required — exact words or phrase to search; no boolean operators, search syntax, or dates

companyPermIds.description: list[string], accepted, one or more company PermIDs

rcsCodes.description: accepted, Filter codes for topics, sectors, commodities, geographies, or classifications. Use only codes provided by the caller or context; never invent codes. (e.g Z:123, X:456)

start.description: string, accepted, start date (ISO 8601 format, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ | YYYY-MM-DD)

end.description: string, accepted, end date (ISO 8601 format, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ | YYYY-MM-DD)

headlineOnly.description: Optional: Set to true to return only headlines without full story text. Default is false (returns full story text).

tools.name: historical_pricing_summaries
tools.title: Historical Pricing Summaries
tools.description: To retrieve time series pricing Interday summaries data or Intraday summaries data(i.e. bar data). The default timeout is 3 minutes.

universe.description: The instrument identifier as a RIC name or PermID. For FX spot rates you MUST apply these conversion rules before passing the value — do NOT pass the raw currency pair name as typed by the user: (1) When the currency pair includes USD (regardless of whether USD is the base or the quote), pass only the non‑USD currency followed by = — for example EURUSD or USDEUR must become EUR=, USDJPY or JPYUSD must become JPY=. (2) When neither currency is USD (user says EURGBP, EURJPY, GBPJPY, etc.) you MUST pass the full pair with '=' appended — for example EURGBP must become EURGBP=, EURJPY must become EURJPY=. (3) For all other non-FX instruments pass the RIC as-is, for example IBM.N, AAPL.O, .SPX. (4) If the RIC contains the '/' character it must be percent-encoded as %2F, for example aITCPISPGD/C must become aITCPISPGD%2FC.

interval.description: The native or consolidation interval in ISO8601. The supported intervals:PT1M, PT5M, PT10M, PT30M, PT60M, PT1H for intraday summaries; P1D, P7D, P1W, P1M, P3M, P12M, and P1Y for interday summaries.  The default value is P1D

tenor.description: Lookback period from today using market tenor notation (e.g., '1D' for yesterday, '10D' for 10 days, '1W' for 1 week, '3M' for 3 months, '1Y' for 1 year). The server calculates the actual dates. Default: '1D' for intraday intervals (PT1M, PT5M, PT10M, PT30M, PT60M, PT1H), '1M' for interday intervals (P1D, P7D, P1W, P1M, P3M, P12M, P1Y).

start.description: Optional: Explicit start of the query is in ISO8601 with local date only(YYYY-MM-DD) if interval is in [P1D, P7D, P1W, P1M, P3M, P12M, and P1Y] or Explicit start date and timestamp of the query is in ISO8601 with UTC only(YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ, e.g 2018-12-24T09:00:00.000000000Z) if interval is in [PT1M, PT5M, PT10M, PT30M, PT60M, PT1H]. Only use if user specifies an exact date. Otherwise use tenor.

end.description: Optional: Explicit end of the query is in ISO8601 with local date only(YYYY-MM-DD) if interval is in [P1D, P7D, P1W, P1M, P3M, P12M, and P1Y] or Explicit end date and timestamp of the query is in ISO8601 with UTC only(YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ, e.g 2018-12-24T09:00:00.000000000Z) if interval is in [PT1M, PT5M, PT10M, PT30M, PT60M, PT1H]. Only use if user specifies an exact date. Defaults to today.

count.description: Maximum record threshold for response shaping. Max value is 500. If response size is less than or equal to count, the response is unchanged. If response size exceeds count, only the first count records are returned.

tools.name: fixed_income_bond_reference
tools.title: Fixed Income: Bond Reference
tools.description:
**BEFORE CALLING: Count identifiers first. MAX 50 IDENTIFIERS PER CALL.** If user has >50 bonds, split into multiple calls BEFORE executing (e.g., 75 bonds = 2 calls: 50 + 25). Do NOT attempt >50 identifiers - it will fail.

          Retrieve bond reference data via YieldBook Bond Indic API. Returns contractual and reference information about bonds without requiring calculations.

          RETURNED INFORMATION:
          - Security type and sector classification
          - Maturity date and coupon details
          - Credit ratings (S&P, Moody's, Fitch)
          - Issuer information and CUSIP/ISIN identifiers
          - Security-specific data (e.g., pool factor for MBS)
          - Payment frequency and day count conventions

          SUPPORTED SECURITY TYPES:
          - Government bonds (Treasury, Agency)
          - Corporate bonds
          - Mortgage-backed securities or similar ties(MBS, RMBS, CMBS)
          - Asset-backed securities (ABS)
          - Municipal bonds
          - Collateralized mortgage obligations (CMO)

          KEY FEATURES:
          - Batch support: Query up to 50 identifiers per request
          - Multiple identifier types: CUSIP, ISIN, generic YieldBook IDs
          - FNMA or GNMA or similar IDENTIFIER FORMAT: If a user provides space-separated notation like FNMA11.100 F or FNMA20.100 BA, change it to FNMA11.100(F) or FNMA20.100(BA) by replacing the space with parenthesis automatically. If FNMA200.100 or similar id is provided without any letter, pass it as is. If ticket has # like N25.1(#1), pass as is.
          - Optional keyword filtering to retrieve specific fields only
          - No calculations required - pure reference data lookup

          USE CASES:
          - Bond identification and basic information lookup
          - Security screening and filtering
          - Portfolio composition analysis
          - Credit rating verification

tools.name: fixed_income_actual_vs_projected
tools.title: Fixed Income: Actual vs Projected
tools.description:
**BEFORE CALLING: Count identifiers first. MAX 5 IDENTIFIERS PER CALL.** If user has >5 bonds, split into multiple calls BEFORE executing (e.g., 12 bonds = 3 calls: 5 + 5 + 2).

Retrieve actual vs projected prepayment data for mortgage-backed securities via YieldBook API. Compares historical actual prepayment speeds against model-projected speeds.
This tool is only for backward looking historical analysis of actual vs projected prepayment. Do not use this tool for forward-looking analysis. If the user asks to run a PY, requests forward-looking/prepayment projections, use fixed_income_risk_analytics instead.

REQUIRED PARAMETER:
- identifiers: Array of up to 5 bond identifiers (CUSIP, ISIN, or YieldBook ID). FNMA or GNMA or similar IDENTIFIER FORMAT: If a user provides space-separated notation like FNMA11.100 F or FNMA20.100 BA, change it to FNMA11.100(F) or FNMA20.100(BA) by replacing the space with parenthesis automatically. If FNMA200.100 or similar id is provided without any letter, pass it as is (no parentheses needed). If ticket has # like N25.1(#1), pass as is.

OPTIONAL PARAMETER:
- idType: type of identifier provided (e.g., "CUSIP", "ISIN", "SecurityIDEntry", etc.). Defaults to "SecurityIDEntry" if not specified.
- prepayType: MBS prepayment model to use. Defaults to "Model" if not specified. Accepted values:
  - "Model" — current production model (default)
  - "ExpModel" - Model 99
  - "NewModel"
  - "OldExpModel"
  - "OldModel"
  - "PreExpModel" — Model 97
  Only one prepayType is accepted per call.

RETURNED INFORMATION:
- Identity fields: CUSIP, ISIN, ticker, description, security type, maturity date, current coupon
- Monthly actual vs projected CPR vector (dataActVsProjVectorList): date, actualCPR, actualCDR, projectedCPR, projectedCDR, projectedVPR, projectedRefi, projectedCurtail, projectedTurnover
- Period summaries (dataActVsProjSummaryList): 1-month, 3-month, 6-month, 12-month, 24-month, and Life aggregates

USE CASES:
1. **Historical prepayment analysis**: View actual CPR/CDR history for MBS pools
2. **Historical projected prepayment speed**: Get model-projected CPR, VPR, refinancing, curtailment, and turnover rates that are returned alongside historical actual observations
3. **Actual vs projected comparison**: Compare realized prepayment speeds against YieldBook model projections to assess model accuracy

SUPPORTED SECURITY TYPES:
- Mortgage-backed securities (MBS, RMBS)
- Collateralized mortgage obligations (CMO)
- Agency pass-throughs (FNMA, GNMA, FHLMC)

KEY FEATURES:
- Batch support: Query up to 5 identifiers per request
- Multiple identifier types: CUSIP, ISIN, generic YieldBook IDs. If user provides multiple identifiers of different types (e.g., one CUSIP and one ISIN), split into separate calls to the tool.
- Decomposed projections: See refi, curtailment, and turnover components separately

DEFAULT: If idType not specified, defaults to 'SecurityIDEntry'. If prepayType not specified, defaults to 'Model'.

IDTYPE NOTE: If user provides multiple identifiers of different types (e.g., one CUSIP and one ISIN), split into separate calls to the tool since only one idType is accepted at a time.

PREPAYTYPE NOTE: Only one prepayType is accepted per call. To compare models or use different models for different groups of identifiers, split into separate calls to the tool.

ASYNC STATUS CHECK: If a previous request was still processing (returned jobRef and requestId), call this same tool with only { "jobRef": "...", "requestId": "..." } to check if results are ready.

EXAMPLE - "Give me the past six months of historical prepayments on security <identifier>"
{"identifiers": ["<identifier>"], "idType": "SecurityIDEntry", "prepayType": "Model"}

EXAMPLE - "Show historical speeds on <identifier 1>, <identifier 2>, and <identifier 3>"
{"identifiers": ["<identifier 1>", "<identifier 2>", "<identifier 3>"], "idType": "SecurityIDEntry", "prepayType": "Model"}

EXAMPLE - "Give me the past six months of Yield Book projected CPRs on CUSIP <identifier>"
{"identifiers": ["<identifier>"], "idType": "CUSIP", "prepayType": "Model"}

EXAMPLE - "Compare historical speeds versus Yield Book Projected speeds on <identifier>"
{"identifiers": ["<identifier>"], "idType": "SecurityIDEntry", "prepayType": "Model"}

EXAMPLE - "Run Yield Book Actual vs Projected on <identifier 1>, <identifier 2>, <identifier 3>, and <identifier 4>"
{"identifiers": ["<identifier 1>", "<identifier 2>", "<identifier 3>", "<identifier 4>"], "idType": "SecurityIDEntry", "prepayType": "Model"}

EXAMPLE - "How did Yield Book projected CPRs compare to historical CPRs on <identifier>"
{"identifiers": ["<identifier>"], "idType": "SecurityIDEntry", "prepayType": "Model"}

EXAMPLE - "Run actual vs projected using Model 99 on <identifier>"
{"identifiers": ["<identifier>"], "idType": "SecurityIDEntry", "prepayType": "ExpModel"}

EXAMPLE - "Compare Model 97 projected speeds against actuals on <identifier>"
{"identifiers": ["<identifier>"], "idType": "SecurityIDEntry", "prepayType": "PreExpModel"}

EXAMPLE - "Run Yieldbook Actual vs Projected for jobRef <jobRef> and requestId <requestId>"
{"jobRef": "<jobRef>", "requestId": "<requestId>"}

tools.title: Fixed Income: Risk Analytics
tools.description:
**If the user specifies yieldbook or YB or yb, use THIS tool (fixed_income_risk_analytics). Do NOT use a QPS tool.**
**If the user says run a PY / do a PY / run py on a bond, use THIS tool.**
**If the user asks for projected speeds, forward-looking speeds, or prepayment projections on a bond or MBS without explicitly asking for actual-vs-projected history, use THIS tool.**

DO NOT USE THIS TOOL for yield curve retrieval (use fixed_income_curves) or rate shock/scenario analysis on bonds (use fixed_income_scenario_analytics).

**BEFORE CALLING: Count bonds first. MAX 50 BONDS PER CALL.** If user has >50 bonds, split into multiple calls BEFORE executing. Do NOT attempt >50 bonds - it will fail.

Calculate bond price/yield metrics via YieldBook PY API. Computes pricing, OAS, duration, convexity, DV01, spreads, and accrued interest.
SUPPORTS: Government, Corporate, MBS/CMBS, ABS, Municipal, Callable/Putable, FRN, TIPS, Bond Future, Swap.

REQUIRED PARAMETERS (per bond):
- identifier: Bond ID (CUSIP, ISIN, or YieldBook ID). FNMA or GNMA or similar IDENTIFIER FORMAT: If a user provides space-separated notation like FNMA11.100 F or FNMA20.100 BA, change it to FNMA11.100(F) or FNMA20.100(BA) by replacing the space with parenthesis automatically. If FNMA200.100 or similar id is provided without any letter, pass it as is (no parentheses needed). If ticket has # like N25.1(#1), pass as is.
- level: Price/yield input like "100" (price), "100d" (dollars), "4.5y" (yield), "75/i" (spread)
- curve: Must include curveType - use "SWAP_RFR" (SOFR, recommended) or "GVT" (government)


MBS/TBA/CMO DEFAULTS — ALWAYS INCLUDE THESE for mortgage-backed securities:
When pricing MBS, TBA, CMO, or ABS bonds (identifiers like FNMA*, FHLMC*, GNMA*, or CUSIPs for MBS pools), you MUST include ALL of the following in the FIRST call:
1. volatility: {"type": "Default"} — required for OAS/option-adjusted calculations on MBS. Omitting this causes a "Volatility model is not defined" error.
2. extraSettings: {"optionModel": "OASEDUR"} — required for spread-based analytics on mortgage bonds.
These two are MANDATORY for MBS. Do NOT omit either of them. Example MBS bond:
{"identifier": "FNMA6.5-TBA", "level": "100", "curve": {"curveType": "SWAP_RFR"}, "volatility": {"type": "Default"}, "extraSettings": {"optionModel": "OASEDUR"}}
NOTE: Do NOT include prepaySettings unless the user explicitly requests a specific prepay model or rate.

OPTIONAL PARAMETERS:
- idType, settlementType, settlementDate, userTag
- prepaySettings (MBS/ABS): ONLY if user requests a specific prepay model/rate. {type, rate}. Types: Model (25.1), OldModel (24.1), CPR (e.g., 6=6% CPR), PSA (e.g., 150=150% PSA). Omit entirely otherwise — API defaults are sufficient.
- volatility: {type, rate}. Use "Default" for standard vol. Other types: LMMSOFR, LMMSkew, Single, Market, etc.
  The "rate" field is ONLY allowed when type is "Single". Pass the user's number exactly as given — do NOT divide by 100.
- globalSettings: pricingDate (YYYY-MM-DD), useLiveData, usePreviousClose (only one date option allowed), retrievePPMProjection (boolean, default false — set to true to retrieve monthly prepayment projections)
- keywords: Array of output fields to include
- extraSettings.includePartials: Set to true to include partial (stub) period cashflows in analytics when user mentions "Calculate Partials", "with Partials on", "with Partial Durations", "Key Rate Durations", or any mention of "Partial", "Partials". Example: {"extraSettings": {"includePartials": true}}. NOTE: ONLY use partialVega if user explicitly says "Partial Vegas" (different from Partial Durations).
- extraSettings.partialVega: Set to true to calculate partial vega outputs if user explicitly requests "Partial Vegas" (NOT Partial Durations). Example: {"extraSettings": {"partialVega": true}}
- extraSettings.volatilityDuration: Set to true to calculate volatility duration. Example: {"extraSettings": {"volatilityDuration": true}}

DATE OPTIONS (mutually exclusive):
- usePreviousClose=true: Use previous market close (default, most stable)
- useLiveData=true: Use live intraday market data
- pricingDate: Use specific historical date

tools.name: cofbox
tools.title: SocGen: CofBox
tools.description:
SocGen CofBox — visualize implied Cost of Funding (COF) levels on equity indices. COF measures the financing cost of holding equity index positions via derivatives (futures, TRS, synthetics).

UNIVERSE: 113 equity indices across EMEA (54), Asia Pacific (20), Americas (27), and Global (12). Standard tier: SX5E, SPX, NKY only.
HISTORY: Up to 15 years of historical data (Premium). Standard tier: 1 week.
DIVIDEND TREATMENTS: CofDiv100pct, CofDivNtr (Standard + Premium), CofDivMarket (Premium only).

SUBTOOLS:
- cofbox_instruments: Discover available instruments, get maturity details, search by underlying/currency/rate. **Call this first.**
- cofbox_analysis: Run COF analysis (Cof, FwdCof, RollDownCof) with different dividend assumptions.

TYPICAL WORKFLOW:
1. Request cofbox_instruments (action 'list') to discover instrument codes
2. Request cofbox_instruments (action 'details') to get maturity codes (listed and running maturities)
3. Request cofbox_analysis (action 'run') with discovered codes

USE CASES:
- Assess if derivatives are trading expensive/cheap vs historical levels
- Take long/short COF position on the term structure
- Choose the optimal derivatives maturity to trade
- Compare financing costs across equity indices and regions
- Identify dislocations and run optimization for carry strategies using historical data
- Analyse dividend assumption sensitivity (100% vs market-implied vs NTR)

USED BY: Hedge Funds, Treasury desks, Insurers, Pension Funds, Risk departments.

Submit a requests array with entries specifying dataType (cofbox_instruments | cofbox_analysis) and matching options. Multiple requests can be combined in a single call for efficiency.

DEFAULTS FOR SMALLER RESPONSES:
- cofbox_analysis defaults omitted analysisTypes to ["Cof"].
- Request FwdCof or RollDownCof only when the user explicitly asks for forward or rolldown analysis.
- cofbox_analysis defaults omitted cofTypes to ["CofDiv100pct"].

TOKEN LIMIT — never call action:"list" without a filter. The full list returns 500+ instruments (~205KB) and can overflow the context window.

REGION-TO-UNDERLYING MAPPING FOR action:"search":
- EMEA / Europe: SX5E, DAX, CAC, AEX, FTSE, IBEX, FTSEMIB
- Americas / US: SPX, INDU, NDX, RTY, IBOV
- Asia Pacific: NKY, HSI, HSCEI, AS51, KOSPI2
- Global / World: MXEF, MXEA, NDDUWI

When the user asks by region, ask: "There are 500+ instruments across EMEA, Americas, Asia Pacific and Global. Which region or index are you interested in?"
Then call action:"search" with a representative underlyingCode instead of action:"list".

CALL EXAMPLE — list all instruments:
{ "requests": [{ "dataType": "cofbox_instruments", "options": { "action": "list" } }] }

CALL EXAMPLE — get maturity codes for SX5E (do this before running analysis):
{ "requests": [{ "dataType": "cofbox_instruments", "options": { "action": "details", "instrumentCodes": ["SX5E_EUR_EON"] } }] }

CALL EXAMPLE — search instruments by underlying index:
{ "requests": [{ "dataType": "cofbox_instruments", "options": { "action": "search", "underlyingCode": "SPX" } }] }

CALL EXAMPLE — list available analysis types and dividend treatments:
{ "requests": [{ "dataType": "cofbox_analysis", "options": { "action": "list_types" } }] }

CALL EXAMPLE — run COF analysis for SX5E June maturity:
{ "requests": [{ "dataType": "cofbox_analysis", "options": { "action": "run", "instruments": [{ "instrumentCode": "SX5E_EUR_EON", "maturitiesCodes": ["Jun25"] }], "analysisTypes": ["Cof"], "cofTypes": ["CofDivNtr"] } }] }

CALL EXAMPLE — discover instruments and run analysis in one call:
{ "requests": [{ "dataType": "cofbox_instruments", "options": { "action": "list" } }, { "dataType": "cofbox_analysis", "options": { "action": "run", "instruments": [{ "instrumentCode": "SX5E_EUR_EON", "maturitiesCodes": ["Jun25"] }], "analysisTypes": ["Cof"], "cofTypes": ["CofDivNtr"] } }] }

options.title: CofBox Analysis Options
options.description:
Run Cost Of Funding (COF) analysis via SocGen CofBox API. COF measures the financing cost of holding equity index positions via derivatives.

ACTIONS:
- 'run' (default): Execute COF analysis for one or more instruments
- 'list_types': Discover available analysis types (no parameters needed)

ANALYSIS TYPES (can combine multiple):
- Cof: Spot Cost Of Financing spread rate — use to assess if derivatives are expensive/cheap vs historical
- FwdCof: Forward spread rates between maturities — use to take long/short COF position on the term structure
- RollDownCof: Rolldown spread rates between maturities — use to choose optimal maturity to trade

DIVIDEND ASSUMPTIONS (cofTypes):
- CofDiv100pct (default): 100% dividend assumption 
- CofDivMarket: Implied from market 
- CofDivNtr: Net Total Return 

HISTORICAL DATA:
- Up to 15 years via startDate/endDate.
- Use date ranges for back-testing carry strategies and identifying dislocations.

USE CASES:
- Compare financing costs across equity indices (multi-instrument in one call)
- Analyse forward COF term structure for scenario building
- Track COF evolution over time with different dividend assumptions
- Identify rolldown opportunities between maturities
- Assess dividend assumption sensitivity (100% vs market vs NTR)

OUTPUT FORMAT:
- Cof: Array of { instrumentCode, maturity, cofRate, date } — plot as line chart (COF Curve) or time series (COF History)
- FwdCof: Matrix [fromMaturity x toMaturity] with forward rates in bps — display as heatmap (COF Forward)
- RollDownCof: Matrix [fromMaturity x toMaturity] with rolldown rates in bps — display as heatmap (COF Rolldown)
Values are in basis points (bps). Negative = cheaper to fund, positive = more expensive.

DEFAULTS FOR SMALLER RESPONSES:
- If analysisTypes is omitted, the tool defaults to ['Cof'] to avoid returning all analysis matrices.
- Request FwdCof and RollDownCof only when explicitly needed.

action.description: Action to perform: 'run' (default, run COF analysis) or 'list_types' (list available analysis types).

analysisTypes.description: Analysis types: 'Cof', 'FwdCof', 'RollDownCof'. Defaults to ['Cof'] when omitted to reduce response size; request FwdCof/RollDownCof explicitly.

cofTypes.description: Dividend assumption types: 'CofDiv100pct', 'CofDivMarket', 'CofDivNtr'. Defaults to ['CofDiv100pct'] when omitted.

startDate.description: Start date for analysis period (format: YYYY-MM-DD). Required by API — auto-defaults to 7 days ago when omitted.

endDate.description: End date for analysis period (format: YYYY-MM-DD). Optional — API defaults to latest available data when omitted.

tools.name: fx_event_tracker
tools.title: SocGen: FX Event Tracker
tools.description:
SocGen FX Event Tracker — analyse historical overnight (O/N) implied volatility around FX market events (central bank meetings, elections, NFP, holidays).

SUBTOOLS:
- fx_event_currency_pairs: List available currency pairs. **Call this first.**
- fx_event_market_events: Discover market events (dates & titles) for a currency pair.
- fx_event_premiums: Compute event premiums (O/N vol difference between event and reference dates), or retrieve historical O/N volatility for single dates or date ranges.

TYPICAL WORKFLOW:
1. Request fx_event_currency_pairs to discover available pairs (e.g., EUR/USD, GBP/USD)
2. Request fx_event_market_events with a currency pair to find upcoming events
3. Request fx_event_premiums (action 'compute') with event date, ref date, and history range

USE CASES:
- Quantify the volatility premium the market prices around scheduled events
- Compare event premium evolution over time for a given currency pair
- Assess if FX options around events are priced cheap/expensive vs history
- Back-test event-driven FX options strategies using historical O/N vol data
- Identify structural patterns in event premiums across different event types

USED BY: FX Options desks, Macro Hedge Funds, Volatility traders, Risk managers.

Submit a requests array with entries specifying dataType (fx_event_currency_pairs | fx_event_market_events | fx_event_premiums) and matching options. Multiple requests can be combined in a single call for efficiency.

DEFAULTS FOR SMALLER RESPONSES:
- fx_event_market_events defaults omitted pageSize to 25.
- fx_event_premiums compute defaults omitted startDate/endDate to a 1-year lookback ending on eventDate.
- Prefer a single compute request unless the user explicitly asks for multiple events or pairs.

CALL EXAMPLE — list available currency pairs:
{ "requests": [{ "dataType": "fx_event_currency_pairs", "options": {} }] }

CALL EXAMPLE — get ECB meeting events for EUR/USD:
{ "requests": [{ "dataType": "fx_event_market_events", "options": { "currencyPair": "EUR/USD", "eventTitle": "ECB", "pageSize": 10 } }] }

CALL EXAMPLE — compute vol premium for a single event (startDate/endDate optional, default 1-year lookback):
{ "requests": [{ "dataType": "fx_event_premiums", "options": { "action": "compute", "requests": [{ "currencyPair": "EUR/USD", "eventDate": "2025-04-17", "refDate": "2025-04-16" }] } }] }

CALL EXAMPLE — historical O/N vol for a date range (note: currencyPair is top-level, NOT inside requests[]):
{ "requests": [{ "dataType": "fx_event_premiums", "options": { "action": "volatility_overnight_range", "currencyPair": "EUR/USD", "volatilityOvernightStartDate": "2025-01-01", "volatilityOvernightEndDate": "2025-04-17" } }] }

CALL EXAMPLE — discover events and compute premium in one call:
{ "requests": [{ "dataType": "fx_event_market_events", "options": { "currencyPair": "EUR/USD" } }, { "dataType": "fx_event_premiums", "options": { "action": "compute", "requests": [{ "currencyPair": "EUR/USD", "eventDate": "2025-04-17", "refDate": "2025-04-16" }] } }] }

Retrieve market events (e.g., central bank meetings, NFP, holidays) for a given currency pair.

Use this to discover upcoming or historical events that affect FX volatility.
Results can be filtered by event title or start date, and paginated via pageSize.

REQUIRED: currencyPair (e.g., 'EUR/USD') — use fx_event_currency_pairs first to discover valid pairs.

DEFAULTS FOR SMALLER RESPONSES:
- pageSize defaults to 25 when omitted.

RETURNED DATA:
